meta.title: ymzz-loop — Your daily review, on a loop
meta.desc: ymzz-loop — multi-end sync for daily review. Auto-backs up yesterday. Each deploy is a 600-day chapter that ends with a 600-day summary; then pause and redeploy for the next chapter. Free MIT.
hero.eyebrow: Product · multi-end sync · by 晏銘湛箴
hero.identity: Write in Notion. Keep every day in Google Sheets and your own GitHub Markdown (optional Feishu). $0 self-host. One deploy = one 600-day chapter that closes with a summary.
intro.h: Less blank page. More day you actually kept.
intro.p1: ymzz-loop is not another place to journal. It is the open-source loop that makes the habit automatic — then hands the archive back to you.
intro.p2: At your chosen time it creates today's blank review in Notion, emails you the link, and auto-backs up yesterday into Google Sheets, Markdown in your fork, and optionally Feishu / Lark.
intro.who.p: Anyone who wants a daily-review habit with multi-end backups — students, traders, builders. You are the product user; every setup step below is for you after you fork.
intro.own.p: Your fork, your Notion, your Sheet, your Markdown. No shared SaaS database. When remaining days hit 0, this chapter closes with a summary and the daily schedule pauses — redeploy for a new chapter.
intro.cost.p: Nothing. Free Actions minutes + free Notion/Google APIs. No AI quota. Chapter length: 600 days, then a summary.
f1.p: Score, mood, energy, Keep / Problem / Try, decisions, top 3 for tomorrow, deep-work hours.
f2.p: Ticker, platform, cost, value, weight, thesis, stop/target — snapshotted daily so you see how it changed. Works for any broker (entered by you).
f3.p: One email linking to the page created in step 01, at the hour you choose, in your own time zone.
f4.p: Yesterday lands in Google Sheets for charts and as Markdown in your repo — a permanent, diffable archive.
f5.p: UTC 07:00 by default. Set two repo Variables and it is yours; filenames carry your zone.
f6.p: Add Obsidian, Telegram, CSV… by dropping in one file.

setup.sub: About 15 minutes, once. Progress is saved only in this browser.
t1.b:
1. Open the GitHub repo and choose Use this template → Create a new repository (or Fork).
  2. Make it Private — your reviews are stored there.

Public repos get unlimited Actions minutes; a private repo uses roughly 720 min/month (24 short runs a day), within GitHub Free's 2,000.
t1.x: No “Use this template” button? Use Fork instead.
t2.b:
1. Open Notion → Integrations → New integration (Internal), name it ymzz, copy the token.
  2. Open the Notion page that should hold your reviews → ⋯ → Connections → add ymzz.
t2.x: setup.sh says “object not found”? The page isn't connected to the integration yet.
t3.b: On your computer (Node.js 20+), create the two blank databases:
t3.x: On Windows use the PowerShell lines below.
t4.b:
1. Google Cloud Console → new project → enable Google Sheets API.
  2. IAM → Service accounts → Create → Keys → Add key → JSON.
  3. Create a Google Sheet and share it with the service-account email as Editor. The part in /d/SHEET_ID/edit is your SHEET_ID.
t4.x: “The caller does not have permission”? The Sheet isn't shared with the service account.
t5.b:
1. Turn on 2-Step Verification for your Google account.
  2. Create one at App passwords — you get a 16-character password.
t5.x: Page not available? 2-Step Verification is off, or a work account blocks it.
t6.b: Repo → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret. Add each name:
t6.x: Secrets stay in your GitHub. Never paste them into a website, including this one.
t7.b: Default is UTC 07:00. Pick yours — for example America/Los_Angeles (Pacific) — and copy the generated settings.
t7.x: GitHub schedules can run a few minutes late; the gate catches up on the next hour.
t8.b:
1. Actions → daily-review → Run workflow.
  2. Success: an email arrives, today's page appears in Notion, and your Sheet gets two tabs.
  3. From now on it runs by itself.
t8.x: A red run? Open it — the failing step names the missing secret. You also get a failure email.

tz.utc: First hourly gate after your time (UTC)
a1: Yes. It runs on GitHub's free Actions minutes and free Notion/Google APIs. There is no paid tier.
a2: In your Notion, your Google account and your repository. This website stores only your language, theme and setup progress in your browser (localStorage). No cookies, no trackers.
a3: You get an email with a link to the failed run. The next hour retries automatically, because a day is only marked done after success.
a4: By design: first success starts a 600-day chapter (countdown 600→0). At 0 the daily loop pauses and the chapter is meant to close with a 600-day summary. Your Notion, Sheets and Markdown stay yours. Deploy a newer ymzz-loop version to open the next 600-day chapter.
a5: Yes — every field is defined in one file, scripts/schema.mjs.

loop.p: A multi-end sync you set up once. GitHub Actions runs it in your fork every day through this 600-day chapter.
loop.1p: At your chosen time, a blank daily-review template is created in your Notion, and you get an email with the link.
loop.2p: Fill in score, mood, Keep / Problem / Try and tomorrow's top 3 — in Notion, on any device.
loop.3p: The next run auto-ingests what you wrote yesterday into Google Sheets and Markdown in your own GitHub fork (optional Feishu).
loop.again: Then it repeats — every day, hands-off — until the chapter ends with a summary.
f7.p: Optional: sync yesterday into your Feishu Bitable (and Docx). Off until you set FEISHU_APP_ID / SECRET.

diff.p: Day One is a lovely journal. Zapier is glue. Obsidian DIY is a project. ymzz-loop is the loop you already own — compared on what is concrete, not on invented benchmarks.
diff.b1: Each deploy is a 600-day chapter ending in a summary — then pause; redeploy for the next chapter
diff.b2: Multi-end by default: Notion + Sheets + own GitHub Markdown (+ Feishu)
diff.b3: Runs in your fork on free Actions — no SaaS rent, no AI quota
hero.promise: A day you never review is a day you don’t get back. Start today.
intro.clarity.p: Open the link in your inbox. Score, mood, keep / problem / try, tomorrow’s three things — ten honest minutes and the day has a shape.
intro.streak.p: The page shows up before you feel like writing. The habit runs on the schedule, not on motivation.
intro.homes.p: Notion to write. Sheets to chart. Markdown in your fork to keep. Yesterday is ingested automatically.
intro.free.p: Free Actions minutes in your own account. No SaaS rent, no AI quota. MIT code — fork it and it is yours.
